question.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>∆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> represents the difference in radii of stationary orbits for <math><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> in a hydrogen atom and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>∆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> represents the difference in radii of stationary orbits for <math><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></math> is

solution.text:
Use the relationship between the radius of an orbit and quantum number n of that orbit.

r4-r3r9-r8=r1×42-r1×32r1×92-r1×82=16-981-64=0.41
